# @xano-sdk/password-reset

> Token-based password reset for a Xano SDK workspace: a single-use token table,
> three public endpoints, and the reset email sent with `s.util.send_email`
> through Resend or Xano's built-in mailer.
> Registers one table (`password_reset_token`), one API group (`Password Reset`), and three
> endpoints (`POST password_reset/request`, `/confirm`, `/validate`) onto a consumer's
> workspace. There is no runtime: every export is a typed def object, and the consumer's
> `Xano` instance does all encoding at `export()`.

**Authentication is not included.** This package resets a password on a table you
already have. Pair it with `@xano-sdk/auth`, or with your own signup/login stack -
it depends on neither.

## Install

```bash
npm install @xano-sdk/password-reset @xano/sdk
```

`@xano/sdk` is a **peer dependency**, range `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0` - one shared copy only, or the
statement and kind registries fork. This package is tested against **1.0.0** exactly:
that is the version its golden bundle fixture was generated against.

What the golden fixture does and does not cover: it freezes the exact bytes this module
encodes to, so a peer bump that changes the encoding fails here rather than in your
workspace. It does **not** cover what the ENGINE does with those bytes - mail delivery and
the Resend account's own rules are outside it, and need a live probe.

`xanosdk marketplace install @xano-sdk/password-reset` (and `xanosdk init --marketplace`) installs
the package but does not write the `registerPasswordReset` call: it needs `authTable`, `resetUrl`
and `fromEmail`, which only you can answer. `init --marketplace` leaves a commented call in
`xano/index.ts` naming the package; fill it in as in the Quickstart below.

Set the Resend key as a **workspace environment variable** named by `apiKeyEnv`
(default `RESEND_API_KEY`). It is read server-side with `env()`, so it is never in
the bundle and cannot reach a frontend build. Declare the NAME with an empty value and keep
the VALUE in the gitignored `xano/.env`; `xanosdk env set RESEND_API_KEY` (value on stdin)
changes the live value without a deploy:

```ts
import { Xano, workspaceConfig } from "@xano/sdk";
const app = new Xano().registerWorkspace(workspaceConfig({ name: "my-app", env: { RESEND_API_KEY: "" } }));
```

⚠ Once a workspace config declares ANY env var, `export()` warns (and `--strict` fails) on every
`env()` name it does not declare. This package reads `RESEND_API_KEY` (or your `apiKeyEnv`),
plus `APP_URL` if you pass `resetUrl: env("APP_URL")` - declare each one you use. There is
nothing to configure for `emailProvider: "xano"`.

## Quickstart

```ts
// xano/index.ts
import { workspace, table, f } from "@xano/sdk";
import { registerPasswordReset } from "@xano-sdk/password-reset";

// Your auth table. @xano-sdk/password-reset never declares one - it points at yours.
const userTable = table({
  name: "user",
  auth: true,
  schema: { email: f.email({ required: true }), password: f.password({ required: true }) },
  index: [{ type: "unique", fields: [{ name: "email" }] }],
});

const app = workspace("my-app").registerTables([userTable]);

// registerPasswordReset RETURNS the def set. It is the only route to the registered defs.
const reset = registerPasswordReset(app, {
  authTable: userTable,
  resetUrl: "https://app.example.com/reset",   // YOUR page. The email links here.
  fromEmail: "no-reply@your-verified-domain.com",
  canonical: "password_reset",
});

export default app;
```

```bash
npx xanosdk export ./xano/index.ts --strict   # compile and check; writes xano/xano.lock beside the entry - commit it
npx xanosdk deploy ./xano/index.ts            # a live ephemeral backend to call
```

The flow, end to end:

1. The user submits their address to `POST password_reset/request`.
2. This module mints a random UUID (v4) token, stores it with an expiry, and mails
   `<resetUrl>?token=<token>`.
3. Your page at `resetUrl` reads `?token=`, optionally calls
   `POST password_reset/validate` to show "this link has expired" before the form,
   and posts the token plus the new password to `POST password_reset/confirm`.
4. The user logs in through your ordinary login endpoint. Confirm mints no session.

## Exports

Values:

- `registerPasswordReset(xano, options)` - builds the def set, registers it, and RETURNS it.
- `createPasswordReset(options)` - builds the def set WITHOUT registering it.
- `DEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT`, `MIN_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS`, `MAX_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS` - the values the
  option gate applies and enforces, so you can widen from a known base.

Types (these erase at compile time - `import type` them and pay no bundle bytes):

- `PasswordResetOptions` / `ResolvedPasswordResetOptions`
- `EmailProvider` (`"resend" | "xano"`), `RateLimitOptions`
- `PasswordResetToken` - one `password_reset_token` row
- `PasswordResetDefs` - what one create call minted
- `RequestResetBody`/`RequestResetResponse`, `ConfirmResetBody`/`ConfirmResetResponse`,
  `ValidateResetBody`/`ValidateResetResponse`

## Endpoints

All three are **public** - a caller who could authenticate does not need any of them.

| Route | Verb | Input | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| `password_reset/request` | POST | `email` (required) | `{ ok: true }`, always |
| `password_reset/validate` | POST | `token` (required) | `{ ok: true, expires_at }`, or 400 |
| `password_reset/confirm` | POST | `token`, `password` (both required, min 8) | `{ ok: true }`, or 400 |

`request` answers `{ ok: true }` for an address with no account, and for one that has
one. That is deliberate: it is unauthenticated, so anything else lets anyone ask it
whether anyone else has an account. Do not "improve" it into a 404.

`validate` and `confirm` return ONE message for an unknown token, a spent token and an
expired one: `"This reset link is not valid. Request a new one."`. Same reason.

**`{ ok: true }` from `request` means the stack ran, NOT that an email was sent.** Nor does
`send_email`'s own `status: "success"`, which means QUEUED and comes back even for a recipient
that is not a valid address - it catches a misconfigured statement and nothing else. This
package deliberately does not branch on it - a caller-visible difference between a failed send and no
send at all is the enumeration oracle again. Watch your provider's logs. Two failures worth
recognising: `"Workspace admin not found"` means the built-in `"xano"` mailer was used on an
ephemeral environment, where it cannot work; `"Missing required field for Send Email."` is
usually an unset `RESEND_API_KEY`, which the engine does not name.

**`emailProvider: "xano"` delivers ONLY to the workspace admin.** Confirmed by a paired send on
a live instance: the admin got their copy, a non-admin never did, and both reported
`status: "success"`. The built-in mailer sends AS the workspace admin, so it can only send TO
them. A password reset mails whoever asked, so `"xano"` silently delivers nothing to every
caller who is not the admin. **Ship on `"resend"`.**

`"xano"` is still the right keyless SMOKE TEST, with one condition: the recipient must be the
workspace admin. If you are the admin of the instance - common when building on your own
workspace - set `emailProvider: "xano"`, request a reset for your own address, and the mail
arrives with no account, no key and no domain. If you are not the admin, test against the
admin's address or use your own Resend key; any other address looks like it worked and
delivers nothing.

Resend's sandbox sender `onboarding@resend.dev` needs no verified domain and delivers only to
the address the Resend ACCOUNT is registered under - a good second test, and not a deployment
sender. For real traffic, verify your own domain in Resend, send from it, and put `resetUrl`
on it: a shared sandbox sender plus a "Reset your password" subject plus a link to an
unrelated domain is close to a textbook phishing signature, and gets filtered.

## Options

| Option | Default | Why the default is what it is |
|---|---|---|
| `authTable` | **required** | The table whose password is reset. Pass the def HANDLE, not a name - a bare name cannot be resolved to a guid and the column deploys dangling. |
| `resetUrl` | **required** | Your page. The email links to `<resetUrl>?token=<token>` (`&token=` if it already has a query string). Must be http(s); any other scheme is refused, because the link goes into mail a stranger can cause to be sent. Takes a string (resolved at EXPORT time, so it cannot address a `deploy --static` host) or a `Value` such as `env("APP_URL")`, resolved at REQUEST time - see *On an EPHEMERAL, point `resetUrl` at your local dev server*. |
| `fromEmail` | **required for Resend** | Resend refuses a sender on an unverified domain, and that failure surfaces at send time - on a real user's reset. Optional for `"xano"`. |
| `emailProvider` | `"resend"` | `"xano"` is the built-in mailer: no key, no verified sender, no configuration. Right for a prototype and for a test that must not depend on a third-party account. |
| `apiKeyEnv` | `"RESEND_API_KEY"` | Read server-side with `env()`. Ignored for `"xano"`. |
| `tokenTtlSeconds` | `3600` | Bounded 60s..7d. A reset token is a bearer credential for one account, so an unbounded lifetime is a second password sitting in an inbox. |
| `rateLimit` | `{ max: 5, ttl: 900 }` | Every endpoint here is unauthenticated, one SENDS MAIL, and the other two are the brute-force surface for a token that changes a password. `false` is the explicit opt-out; the step stays in the stack, disabled. |
| `emailSubject` / `emailIntro` / `emailOutro` | sensible English | The default intro names the expiry in minutes. `emailSubject` is also the heading. |
| `emailFormat` | `"html"` | The styled document. `"text"` for plain text. The engine has ONE `message` field, so an HTML send carries no plain-text alternative. |
| `emailButtonLabel` | `"Choose a new password"` | HTML only. |
| `brandName` | unset | Short product name above the heading; the block is omitted entirely when unset. |
| `brandColor` | `"#18181b"` | Button and link colour, hex only - it lands in a `style` attribute. Button text is white, so a pale accent is unreadable. |
| `emailColumn` / `passwordColumn` | `"email"` / `"password"` | Checked against `authTable`'s schema at option time, so a wrong name is a sentence rather than a stack trace through the encoder. |
| `canonical` | unset | Identity belongs to your `xano.lock`. Pin it when you need `getPath()` to resolve in a browser bundle with no lock file. |
| `history` | `false` | Request history stores the request BODY - here that is a reset token and a plaintext new password. |

## The email

HTML by default: one card, a heading, the intro, a button, the link again as copyable text, and
the outro under a rule. Table-based with inline styles (Outlook renders through Word's HTML
engine), and dark mode as a `prefers-color-scheme` override on top of the inline light styles.

The link appears in the document **three** times over - the button's `href`, the fallback
anchor's `href`, and that anchor's visible text - all joined at runtime by the filter chain.
Every consumer-supplied string is HTML-escaped into it at build time.

Do not rebuild this document yourself with `c.text(...)` and a template literal: a template
literal cannot compose a tagged value, so `` c.text(`…${ref("token")}…`) `` type-checks and
mails `[object Object]`. If you need a different design, change the parts in
`src/api/email-template.ts` - they are joined around the token, never interpolated.

## Calling the endpoints from a typed client

```ts
import type { ConfirmResetBody, ConfirmResetResponse } from "@xano-sdk/password-reset";

const res = await fetch(`${XANO_HOST}/api:password_reset/password_reset/confirm`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ token, password } satisfies ConfirmResetBody),
});
const done: ConfirmResetResponse = await res.json();
```

The path's `api:` token is the API group's **canonical**. Pin it through the `canonical`
option and the path is knowable from source alone; leave it unset and it comes from your
`xano.lock` after the first export.

No `Authorization` header on any of the three - they are public by design.

## Working with an auth table

`authTable` takes **any** table def handle. This package declares no user table and depends on
no other package - it points at whatever you already have.

What it requires of that table, and nothing else:

| | |
|---|---|
| `table({ auth: true })` | so your login endpoint can mint tokens against it. This module never reads or mints one. |
| an address column | default `"email"`; rename with `emailColumn`. |
| an **`f.password()`** column | default `"password"`; rename with `passwordColumn`. |

**The password column must be `f.password()`, and this is checked.** The confirm endpoint
writes the submitted password as PLAINTEXT and relies on the COLUMN to hash it on write. An
`f.text()` column would store every reset password in the clear - deploying clean, answering
200, with no symptom but a readable database - so `resolveOptions` refuses it by name. Both
column names are checked against the table's schema too, and both are reported at once.

### With `@xano-sdk/auth`

Its defaults are already the ones this module expects, so there is nothing to configure:

```ts
import { workspace } from "@xano/sdk";
import { registerAuth, userTable } from "@xano-sdk/auth";
import { registerPasswordReset } from "@xano-sdk/password-reset";

const app = registerAuth(workspace("my-app"), { canonical: "authn" });

registerPasswordReset(app, {
  authTable: userTable,                          // auth's own handle - not a name
  resetUrl: "https://app.example.com/reset",
  fromEmail: "no-reply@your-verified-domain.com",
  canonical: "password_reset",
});

export default app;
```

Verified on a real consumer install of both packages: the two API groups coexist, no guid
collides, `auth/signup`, `auth/login` and `auth/me` are untouched, and the token table's `owner`
resolves to auth's `user` guid.

⚠ `@xano-sdk/auth` is a SINGLETON-shaped module - its api group is a module-level def, shared
process-wide - so `registerAuth` can be called **once per process**. A test file that builds two
workspaces both using it fails on the second, with a message about canonicals rather than about
what you did. `@xano-sdk/password-reset` is factory-shaped and has no such limit.

### With your own auth table

Name the columns if they differ. Nothing else changes:

```ts
const members = table({
  name: "member",
  auth: true,
  schema: {
    login_email: f.email({ required: true }),
    secret: f.password({ required: true }),   // f.password, not f.text
  },
  index: [{ type: "unique", fields: [{ name: "login_email" }] }],
});

registerPasswordReset(app, {
  authTable: members,
  emailColumn: "login_email",
  passwordColumn: "secret",
  resetUrl: "https://app.example.com/reset",
  fromEmail: "no-reply@your-verified-domain.com",
});
```

Your own login endpoint keeps working unchanged - this module only ever WRITES the password
column, and it mints no session. After a reset the user signs in through whatever you already
had.

## Wiring a React frontend

This package ships **no frontend files** - it is def objects only. What follows is the whole
integration, and it is short on purpose.

You need ONE page. It does two jobs depending on whether the URL carries a `?token=`: without
one it collects an address; with one it collects a new password. That page's URL is the
`resetUrl` option, and the email links to `<resetUrl>?token=<token>`.

### On an EPHEMERAL, point `resetUrl` at your local dev server

A string `resetUrl` is resolved at **export** time - it is baked into the email body as a
build-time constant. `xanosdk deploy --static` mints a **NEW static host on every run**, so on an ephemeral
environment the link can never address the frontend that is currently serving: deploy N can only
carry deploy N-1's URL, and there is no ordering that fixes it.

Verified, including the obvious escape route, which does not exist:

```
deploy --static      -> https://5ndw94-....dev.xano.io   200
deploy (no --static) -> that same static host now        404   <- the frontend is GONE
deploy --static      -> https://hfplbv-....dev.xano.io   200   (a different URL again)
```

A deploy **without** `--static` REMOVES the frontend; it does not leave it alone. So "deploy
--static to learn the host, then redeploy the backend carrying that host" takes the whole app
down.

Do this instead:

```ts
resetUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:5173/",   // your local dev server, against the deployed backend
```

Run the UI locally against the ephemeral backend and have the page read `?token=` from the app
root, so no history fallback is needed. Pass the real, stable frontend URL only when you deploy
to an instance workspace whose frontend URL does not move.

### Or resolve `resetUrl` at REQUEST time

`resetUrl` also takes a `Value`, which the stack reads when the mail is sent rather than when
the workspace is built:

```ts
import { env } from "@xano/sdk";

registerPasswordReset(app, { authTable: userTable, resetUrl: env("APP_URL"), fromEmail });
```

Declare `APP_URL` in `workspaceConfig({ env })`. Once a `--static` deploy has minted its host,
set the variable on the running backend - no redeploy, so the static host stays up:

```bash
printf %s "https://<the-static-host>/" | npx xanosdk env set APP_URL
```

The emailed link then addresses the frontend that is actually serving. Repeat it after every
`--static` deploy, since each one mints a new host. Three constraints come with the runtime
form, and NONE of them can be checked at build time:

- **No query string.** The `?`-vs-`&` separator depends on the URL's content, which a compiler
  cannot read, so the runtime form always appends `?token=`. `https://app.example.com/reset` is
  fine; `.../reset?ref=email` would produce two `?`.
- **No scheme check.** The `http:`/`https:` refusal runs on a string only. Whatever the variable
  holds goes into the mail, so write access to that variable is write access to a link your
  users are asked to trust.
- **Not HTML-escaped.** In `emailFormat: "html"` the value lands in an `href` and in the visible
  link text unescaped - a build-time escape cannot reach a runtime value. A `"` in the variable
  breaks the attribute.

A plain string stays the right answer wherever the frontend URL is stable: it is validated,
escaped, and folded into the document, so it emits the identical bundle it always has.

⚠ A `release`/`promote` is **ADD-ONLY** on the workspace environment - it creates a variable that
does not exist and will not update one that does. Change `APP_URL` with `xanosdk env set`, not by
releasing again.

`src/lib/passwordReset.ts` - the three calls:

```ts
// `window.XANO_HOST` is injected into every HTML document by `xanosdk deploy --static` (or
// `xanosdk publish <dir>`), before the app bundle runs. In local dev nothing injects it, so the fallback answers.
const HOST = (typeof window !== "undefined" && window.XANO_HOST) || import.meta.env.VITE_XANO_HOST || "";

// The `api:` token is the API group's CANONICAL - the `canonical` option you passed.
const url = (route: string) => `${HOST}/api:password_reset/password_reset/${route}`;

async function post<T>(route: string, body: unknown): Promise<T> {
  const res = await fetch(url(route), {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  });
  const payload = await res.json().catch(() => ({}));
  // Every message this module produces is authored and safe to show a user.
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(payload.message ?? "Something went wrong.");
  return payload as T;
}

export const requestReset  = (email: string) => post<{ ok: true }>("request", { email });
export const validateToken = (token: string) => post<{ ok: true; expires_at: number }>("validate", { token });
export const confirmReset  = (token: string, password: string) => post<{ ok: true }>("confirm", { token, password });
```

The page, in outline:

```tsx
const token = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get("token");

// No token -> collect an address, then show the SAME confirmation either way.
// With a token -> validateToken() on mount, THEN render the password form.
// On success -> send them to your ordinary login page.
```

Type the bodies from this package rather than by hand - the types erase at compile time, so
`import type` costs no bundle bytes:

```ts
import type { ConfirmResetBody, ValidateResetResponse } from "@xano-sdk/password-reset";
```

⚠ `import type` only. Importing a def VALUE for `getPath()` pulls the SDK runtime into the
browser bundle - a ~267 kB (~65 kB gzipped) floor for the first def. For paths as plain data, run
`xanosdk routes ./xano/index.ts --emit xano/routes.gen.ts` and import from that instead.

Five rules for the page. Each one is a property of the endpoints, not a preference:

1. **After `requestReset`, show the same screen for every address.** Do not check whether the
   account exists, and do not say "no account found" - the endpoint refuses to tell you
   precisely so that the page cannot leak it. Say "if that address has an account, a link is on
   its way".
2. **Call `validateToken` on mount, before rendering the password fields.** Otherwise the user
   types a new password twice and only then learns the link expired. That endpoint exists for
   this, and it does not spend the token.
3. **The token goes in a POST body and nowhere else.** Do not store it, do not put it in a
   header, do not write it back into the URL or into analytics. Read it once from the query
   string and hold it in memory.
4. **`confirm` mints no session.** Resetting a password is not logging in. Send the user to your
   login page afterwards; do not fake a signed-in state.
5. **Show the server's message verbatim on a rejection.** All three rejections share one
   sentence by design - do not map them to more specific ones in the UI, which would undo it.

CORS needs no configuration: the engine answers the preflight from any origin, so a frontend on
a static host and a backend on the instance work together as-is.

## Constraints for agents (read before using)

- **Call `registerPasswordReset` ONCE per `Xano` instance.** A second call is refused by name. It
  would otherwise register defs sharing names and fail at `export()` naming neither call site.
- **Pass `authTable` as a def handle**, never a string. `f.tableRef` resolves the target's guid
  eagerly, at column-construction time.
- **Register your auth table yourself.** This package points at it and does not own it, so
  `export()` refuses until you have registered it too.
- **Keep the value `registerPasswordReset` returns.** It is the only route to the registered defs;
  this package exports no module-level def.
- **The `request` endpoint's constant `{ ok: true }` is a security property, not a stub.**
  Making it 404 on an unknown address turns it into an account enumeration oracle.
- **Do not narrow the three rejection messages on `confirm`/`validate` into distinct ones.**
  "Not found", "expired" and "already used" are an oracle about tokens the caller does not hold.
- **Do not add a token to the `confirm` response.** Resetting a password is not logging in; the
  user goes through your ordinary login endpoint next.
- **Tell the consumer to turn OFF click tracking on the sending domain.** Every major provider
  rewrites links through a tracking domain with the original URL - and the TOKEN - encoded in the
  path (`…awstrack.me/L0/https:%2F%2F…%3Ftoken=<token>/1/…`, observed in a real Resend send).
  That both breaks the link for anyone running a blocker AND hands a bearer credential for the
  account to a third party, which undoes the internal column, the single use and the expiry at a
  stroke. This module cannot prevent it - `s.util.send_email` has no per-send tracking flag - so
  it is a setting the consumer must change, and one worth raising unprompted. Same for a URL
  shortener or a "safe links" gateway.
- **Set `apiKeyEnv`'s variable in the WORKSPACE environment, never in the bundle.** Declare the
  name empty in `workspaceConfig({ env })`, keep the value in `xano/.env`, and change it live with
  `xanosdk env set`. A static host serves everything injected into a frontend build
  (`--static-env` included), so a key there is public.
- **`rateLimit: false` is an opt-out you must be able to defend.** The request endpoint sends
  mail on an unauthenticated call - it costs money and it lands in someone else's inbox.
- **Do not pin a guid, and do not pass a `canonical` you are not prepared to keep.** A canonical
  is a public URL token; changing it moves every path in the wild.
- **Request history is OFF, deliberately.** It stores request bodies. Do not turn it on to debug
  and leave it on.
- **Identity is yours, not this package's.** Commit your `xano.lock`: object guids derive from
  `(type, name)`, so a rename without the lock makes the engine DELETE and recreate the object
  rather than renaming it - losing its rows.
- **Never re-export this module's defs from your own `register*` function.** Register them once,
  on one instance.
